# Federal Judge Finds Disenfranchisement is ‘Plausibly Likely and Imminent’ Due to Executive Order Restricting Mail Voting


## U.S. District Court in Massachusetts rules that voting rights group have standing and valid constitutional claims to move forward with a challenge to the executive order


Case


:[League of Women Voters of Massachusetts v. Trump](https://www.aclu.org/cases/league-of-women-voters-of-massachusetts-v-trump)

BOSTON – A U.S. District Court in Massachusetts[ruled](https://www.aclum.org/app/uploads/2026/04/Memorandum-and-Order-7.22.26.pdf) today that nonpartisan voting rights groups have standing and valid constitutional and statutory claims to move forward with a challenge to President Trump’s executive order (EO) restricting mail-in voting.


The court reiterated[earlier holdings](https://www.aclum.org/press-releases/voting-rights-groups-applaud-ruling-declaring-2026-executive-order-interference-with-voter-rolls-and-mail-in-ballots-unconstitutional-and-unlawful/) that parts of the executive order are unconstitutional because they improperly insert the executive branch into elections, interfering with the authority of states and Congress. Among other provisions, the executive order unlawfully directs the United States Postal Service (USPS) to refuse to transmit eligible voters’ ballots.


The executive order has sown confusion and fear and has significantly disrupted the core of the voting rights groups’ work — to educate voters and prepare them to cast ballots. The court acknowledged this burden and added that the groups’ members “will plausibly be harmed by the EO’s implementation because those members include individuals who must rely on mail voting as they live overseas, reside out of state, have disabilities, or are unable to travel to the polls and vote in person.” The court found it “plausibly likely and imminent” that the groups’ members would be disenfranchised in the upcoming election due to the executive order.


The ruling denied, in large part, the federal government and intervenor defendants’ motions to dismiss. That allows the case to move forward, including the groups’[renewed motion](https://www.aclum.org/press-releases/voting-rights-preliminary-injunction-executive-order-restricting-mail-in-ballots/) for a preliminary injunction to block portions of the executive order. A hearing on that motion has been scheduled for Aug. 7, 2026.


The lawsuit was filed by the League of Women Voters of Massachusetts, the League of Women Voters, Association of Americans Resident Overseas (AARO), U.S. Vote Foundation, OCA – Asian Pacific American Advocates (OCA), and Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.


They are represented by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), ACLU of Massachusetts, Brennan Center for Justice at NYU Law, Legal Defense Fund (LDF), Asian Americans Advancing Justice – AAJC (Advancing Justice – AAJC), and LatinoJustice PRLDEF.


**The plaintiffs and their legal counsel issued the following statement:**


“With the November election around the corner, the voting rights groups who filed this lawsuit should be deeply immersed in the vital work of ensuring that their members — and all eligible voters — are prepared to cast their ballots. Instead, the groups have had to limit their voter outreach and spend considerable time and money on revising materials and counseling members who are confused and fearful about the executive order’s impact on their right to vote.


“We are pleased that the court recognized the disruption and chaos caused by the executive order and ruled that our clients’ claims can move forward. We are committed to fighting this unconstitutional and unlawful executive order and to protecting the right to vote, including the ability to vote by mail.”


A copy of the court’s ruling can be found here:[https://www.aclum.org/app/uploads/2026/04/Memorandum-and-Order-7.22.26.pdf](https://www.aclum.org/app/uploads/2026/04/Memorandum-and-Order-7.22.26.pdf)

### League of Women Voters of Massachusetts v. Trump


On March 31, 2026, President Trump issued a sweeping Executive Order titled “Ensuring Citizen Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections,” seeking once again to seize control of election administration from Congress and the states. The Order directs federal agencies to compile lists of U.S. citizens and transmit them to states before every election, directs the U.S. Postal Service — an independent agency established by Congress — to create a list of “approved” mail voters, and instructs USPS to refuse to deliver ballots from voters not on that federally created list. If implemented, the Order would threaten the ability of millions of eligible citizens to cast their ballots, particularly military members, overseas citizens, the elderly, recently naturalized citizens, and voters with disabilities who rely on mail voting.

### ACLU Sues to Stop Unlawful Federal Intimidation of Naturalized Citizen Voters


CALIFORNIA — A coalition of civil rights groups today filed a federal lawsuit to stop an unlawful and discriminatory program by United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) that systematically targets, investigates, and intimidates naturalized U.S. citizens. The lawsuit was filed on behalf of OCA-Asian Pacific American Advocates, OCA-San Mateo, OCA-Sacramento, and Common Cause, represented by the ACLU Voting Rights Project, Asian Americans Advancing Justice – AAJC, ACLU of Northern California, ACLU of Southern California, and Asian Americans Advancing Justice Southern California (AJSOCAL). Since August 2026, USCIS has run what it calls an “Unlawful Voter Initiative” aimed at tracking and investigating foreign-born citizens under the guise of voter eligibility checks. As part of this initiative, federal agents rely on outdated, error-prone data and questionable methods — including posing as individual voters to search private voter registration records on state election websites. As a result, thousands of fully naturalized American citizens are subjected to improper investigations, door-to-door interrogations, and potential disenfranchisement based on flawed government data. “The Trump administration is challenging voters and threatening states based off flawed and outdated data,” said Theresa J. Lee, senior staff attorney with the ACLU’s Voting Rights Project. “These allegations are putting eligible voters — including naturalized U.S. citizens — at risk of disenfranchisement. The administration can’t keep creating political stunts to sow distrust in our elections and lay the groundwork to question results they don’t like. We’re challenging both these unlawful actions and the unreliable data behind them, and we will fight to ensure that no eligible voter is targeted or silenced because of it.” The lawsuit aims to immediately stop the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) from continuing the Unlawful Voter Initiative. It also seeks to block the federal government from pressuring state election officials to withhold or discard valid ballots cast by individuals appearing on DHS’s unreliable lists. Additionally, the legal action demands a formal declaratory judgment establishing that the initiative violates the Civil Rights Act’s Uniform Standards Provision, the Privacy Act, and the Administrative Procedure Act (APA). “Our communities have spent generations fighting to overcome barriers to the ballot box, and we cannot allow government intimidation to become another obstacle,” said Thu Nguyen, executive director of OCA-Asian Pacific American Advocates. “Instead of helping voters participate in our elections, federal agencies are using flawed information to investigate and intimidate the very people they are supposed to serve. These actions threaten to undermine years of progress in building trust and encouraging civic participation in immigrant communities. We cannot allow fear to keep people from exercising their right to vote.” “This administration knows its data is flawed and unreliable, but they’re using it anyway to scare eligible voters away from the polls. It’s a deliberate effort to spread unfounded lies and make people doubt our elections,” said Virginia Kase Solomon, president and CEO of Common Cause. “When even one voter is targeted, all of us are at risk. Common Cause will keep fighting in the courtroom and in our communities to make sure every single eligible voter can cast their ballot without fear of government harassment.” “Naturalized citizens are U.S. citizens, with exactly the same right to vote as anyone born here,” said John C. Yang, president and executive director of Asian Americans Advancing Justice – AAJC. “The ‘Unlawful Voter Initiative’ was never designed to confirm citizenship, and election officials have found it erroneously flagging eligible voters. Purging or investigating voters based on their system errors punishes citizens for the government’s own mistakes. Asian American voters, many of whom are naturalized, are bearing the brunt of it. We are suing to send a message that no eligible voter should be subjected to this intimidation tactic. We urge voters to go to the polls. Do not stay home out of fear.” “Citizenship earned through naturalization is not second-class citizenship. Yet this administration is combing through immigration records to single out naturalized Americans, many of them Asian American and Pacific Islander, and to treat their right to vote as suspect. No other voters face this scrutiny. We are proud to stand with OCA and Common Cause to insist that every eligible voter, however they became a citizen, is treated equally under the law,” said Dahni Tsuboi, CEO of Asian Americans Advancing Justice Southern California. View a copy of the lawsuit here: https://assets.aclu.org/live/uploads/2026/10/001-OCA-v-DHS-Complaint.pdf

### United States v. Alaska


Representing two Alaska voters, the League of Women Voters of Alaska, and Common Cause, the American Civil Liberties Union and ACLU of Alaska moved to intervene in United States v. Alaska, a frivolous lawsuit seeking to prevent from the State of Alaska from certifying its election results if the incumbent U.S. Senator does not win the election. The lawless suit asserts a single claim based on the purpose language of the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA), that has no basis in any case, legal principle, or arguably tenable reading of the NVRA. We are seeking dismissal of this suit that aims to deprive Alaskans of their right to vote and right to representation.
